chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made zakat obligatory just as He made salat (prayer) obligatory.
So if a man were to carry the zakat and give it openly, there would be no blame upon him in that.
That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has apportioned for the poor, within the wealth of the rich, that by which they may be sufficiently provided.
And if He knew that what He had apportioned for them would not suffice them, He would have increased it for them.
Rather, the poor are only afflicted regarding what they receive because of the withholding of those who withhold their rights from them, not because of the ordained obligation.”

key_terms.أَمْوَالِ الْأَغْنِيَاءِ: the wealth of the affluent, from which the poor’s due is assigned
key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: the obligatory alms-tax due upon wealth
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the obligatory salat (prayer), used here as a comparison for the firmness of zakat’s obligation
key_terms.الْفُقَرَاءِ: the poor, who possess a right in the wealth of the rich
key_terms.حُقُوقَهُمْ: their rightful dues that are owed to them
key_terms.عَلَانِيَةً: openly and publicly, without blame in this context

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say that poverty results from withholding zakat rather than from any insufficiency in the obligation itself?
ai.summary: This hadith states that zakat is an obligation established by Allah just like salat (prayer). It explains that the poor have a divinely assigned right in the wealth of the rich, and that poverty persists because people withhold these rights, not because the divine obligation itself is insufficient.
